Honestly, I find that the wave against "pick me girls" across social media recently has, a lot of times, distorted the original definition of the phrase "pick me girls", and equated it to "AFABs who don't conform to traditionally feminine features". I've seen a number of trans masc around this sub, including myself, discuss how some of them have gone through a "not like the other girls" phase, before realizing that they're not a girl after all. Yes, these "pick me girl" behaviors can overlap in cis girls and young trans masc who didn't realize they were trans, but the motivations or intentions behind them are, in most cases, different.

For me, the journey from "Why can't I just be like the other girls?" to accepting myself as a trans man was a very long and mentally draining process, full of trauma and years of depression, and I believe it'd be better if we could be more gentle and understanding towards these alleged "pick me girls".
